findings.title: SQL Injection Vulnerability in Login Function
findings.description: The application's login functionality is susceptible to SQL Injection. An attacker can bypass authentication by injecting malicious SQL queries into the email field, potentially gaining unauthorized access to the application.
findings.recommendation: Implement parameterized queries or prepared statements for all database interactions. Ensure proper input validation and sanitization for user-supplied data.

findings.title: Reflected Cross-Site Scripting (XSS) via Search Parameter
findings.description: The search functionality does not properly sanitize user input, allowing for reflected Cross-Site Scripting (XSS) attacks. An attacker can inject arbitrary client-side scripts, leading to session hijacking, defacement, or redirection.
findings.recommendation: Implement strict input validation and output encoding for all user-supplied data. Consider implementing a Content Security Policy (CSP) to mitigate XSS risks.

findings.title: Insecure Direct Object Reference (IDOR) in User Profile API
findings.description: The application's API endpoint for user profiles allows direct access to user data by incrementing user IDs without proper authorization checks. This enables an attacker to view or modify other users' sensitive information.
findings.recommendation: Implement robust authorization checks on all API endpoints that reference objects directly. Use indirect object references (e.g., UUIDs or hashed IDs) that are harder to guess.

findings.title: Missing Content Security Policy (CSP)
findings.description: The Content Security Policy (CSP) header is not set. CSP helps to prevent cross-site scripting (XSS) and other code injection attacks by specifying which dynamic resources are allowed to load. Without CSP, the browser has no guidance on which sources are trusted, making the application more susceptible to client-side attacks.
findings.recommendation: Implement a strict Content Security Policy (CSP) header. Define trusted sources for scripts, styles, images, and other resources. For example: `Content-Security-Policy: default-src 'self'; script-src 'self' 'unsafe-inline' 'unsafe-eval'; style-src 'self' 'unsafe-inline'; img-src 'self' data:;` (adjust for specific application needs, avoiding 'unsafe-inline' and 'unsafe-eval' where possible).

findings.title: SQL Injection Vulnerability via 'id' parameter
findings.description: The 'id' GET parameter on the Juice Shop application is vulnerable to SQL Injection. This allows an attacker to execute arbitrary SQL commands on the backend database. This can lead to unauthorized data access (e.g., user credentials, order details), data manipulation, authentication bypass, and potentially remote code execution depending on the database configuration and underlying operating system.
findings.recommendation: Implement parameterized queries (prepared statements) for all database interactions. Strictly validate and sanitize all user input to prevent malicious data from reaching the database. Apply the principle of least privilege to database users. Use an ORM that handles query sanitization automatically.

findings.title: Known Default Administrator Credentials
findings.description: The Juice Shop application uses known default administrator credentials (admin@juice-sh.op:admin123) for the primary admin account. An attacker can use these credentials to gain full administrative access to the application, bypassing authentication and potentially compromising data, users, and system integrity.
findings.recommendation: Immediately change the password for the 'admin@juice-sh.op' account to a strong, unique, and complex value. Implement a policy to prevent the use of default or easily guessable credentials for all user accounts, especially privileged ones. Consider disabling or removing default accounts if they are not actively required.
findings.poc:
use auxiliary/scanner/http/http_login
set RHOSTS juice-shop.herokuapp.com
set RPORT 443
set SSL true
set FORM_URI /rest/user/login
set FORM_METHOD POST
set FORM_PARAMS "email=^USER^&password=^PASS^"
set USERNAME admin@juice-sh.op
set PASSWORD admin123
set FORM_SUCCESS "token"
run

findings.title: TLS 1.0 Protocol Enabled
findings.description: The server supports TLS 1.0, an outdated and insecure cryptographic protocol. TLS 1.0 is known to be vulnerable to several attacks (e.g., BEAST) and lacks modern security features. It has been deprecated by the IETF and is not compliant with current PCI DSS requirements.
findings.recommendation: Disable TLS 1.0 support on the server. Configure the server to only support TLS 1.2 and TLS 1.3. Review server configuration files (e.g., Apache's SSLProtocol, Nginx's ssl_protocols) to remove 'TLSv1'.

findings.title: TLS 1.1 Protocol Enabled
findings.description: The server supports TLS 1.1, an outdated cryptographic protocol. While an improvement over TLS 1.0, it still lacks modern security features and is considered insecure by current standards. It has been deprecated by the IETF and is not compliant with current PCI DSS requirements.
findings.recommendation: Disable TLS 1.1 support on the server. Configure the server to only support TLS 1.2 and TLS 1.3. Review server configuration files (e.g., Apache's SSLProtocol, Nginx's ssl_protocols) to remove 'TLSv1.1'.

findings.title: Development Environment Exposed
findings.description: A subdomain for a development environment was discovered. Development environments often contain sensitive information, debug code, unpatched vulnerabilities, or misconfigurations that could be exploited.
findings.recommendation: Securely isolate development environments from public access. Implement strict access controls, IP whitelisting, and ensure no sensitive data or credentials are present. Regularly audit its security posture.

findings.title: Administrative Interface Exposed
findings.description: An administrative subdomain, likely used for managing the application, has been identified. Exposure of such interfaces can lead to unauthorized access, privilege escalation, or full system compromise if not properly secured.
findings.recommendation: Restrict access to administrative interfaces to authorized personnel only, ideally via VPN or IP whitelisting. Implement strong authentication (MFA), robust logging, and regularly monitor for suspicious activity.

findings.title: API Endpoint Discovered
findings.description: An API subdomain was identified, potentially exposing application programming interfaces. APIs can be a vector for data breaches, denial-of-service attacks, or business logic flaws if not properly secured and rate-limited.
findings.recommendation: Conduct a thorough security audit of all exposed API endpoints. Implement strong authentication and authorization, input validation, rate limiting, and robust error handling. Ensure sensitive data is not exposed via API responses.

findings.title: CORS Wildcard
findings.description: The server reflects the 'Origin' header's value in the 'Access-Control-Allow-Origin' header, often combined with 'Access-Control-Allow-Credentials: true'. This allows any origin to perform cross-origin requests with credentials, potentially leading to sensitive data exposure or unauthorized actions if an attacker controls a malicious domain.
findings.recommendation: Implement a strict whitelist of allowed origins. Do not reflect arbitrary 'Origin' header values. Ensure 'Access-Control-Allow-Credentials' is only set to 'true' when strictly necessary and only for explicitly trusted origins. Validate all incoming 'Origin' headers against a predefined list of trusted domains.

findings.title: S3 Bucket Publicly Accessible
findings.description: An S3 bucket named 'juice-shop-prod-logs-bucket', potentially storing application logs or backups, is configured with a public access policy allowing 's3:GetObject' for all users. This could expose sensitive application data, configuration files, or internal operational details to unauthorized parties.
findings.recommendation: Restrict S3 bucket access to only necessary IAM users/roles or specific IP ranges. Enable 'Block Public Access' settings at both the bucket and account level to prevent accidental exposure. Implement bucket policies that enforce least privilege.

findings.title: EC2 Security Group Exposing SSH to Internet
findings.description: The security group 'sg-0abcdef1234567890' (named 'juice-shop-prod-ssh'), associated with EC2 instances running the Juice Shop application, allows inbound traffic on port 22 (SSH) from '0.0.0.0/0'. This exposes the instances to potential brute-force attacks, unauthorized access attempts, and increases the attack surface significantly.
findings.recommendation: Restrict SSH access to specific trusted IP addresses or IP ranges (e.g., corporate VPN, jump box). Consider using AWS Systems Manager Session Manager for secure server access without opening SSH ports directly to the internet.

findings.title: IAM Role for EC2 Instance has S3 Full Access
findings.description: The IAM role 'juice-shop-ec2-role', attached to EC2 instances running the Juice Shop application, has 's3:*' permissions. This violates the principle of least privilege, allowing an attacker who compromises the EC2 instance to potentially access, modify, or delete data in all S3 buckets within the account.
findings.recommendation: Revise the IAM policy for 'juice-shop-ec2-role' to grant only the minimum necessary permissions required for the application's function. If S3 access is needed, specify exact bucket resources and the least privileged actions (e.g., 's3:GetObject' on specific buckets, not 's3:*').

findings.title: K8s Dashboard Exposed
findings.description: The Kubernetes Dashboard is exposed externally without proper authentication or authorization, potentially allowing unauthenticated access to sensitive cluster information, resources, and privileged actions. This could lead to full cluster compromise, data exfiltration, or denial of service within the cluster hosting juice-shop.herokuapp.com.
findings.recommendation: Implement strict network policies (e.g., NetworkPolicies, Ingress rules) to restrict access to the Kubernetes Dashboard only from trusted internal networks or specific IP ranges. Ensure strong RBAC is configured to limit permissions. If external access is required, enforce robust authentication (e.g., OIDC, SAML) and authorization. Consider removing the Dashboard if not strictly necessary for operations.

findings.title: BOLA / IDOR (Broken Object Level Authorization / Insecure Direct Object Reference)
findings.description: The API endpoint `/api/Users/{id}` allows unauthenticated or unauthorized users to access sensitive information of other users by simply changing the user ID in the URL. By iterating through user IDs, an attacker can enumerate and retrieve details such as email addresses, roles, and potentially other profile information for all registered users, bypassing intended authorization controls.
findings.recommendation: Implement robust authorization checks at the API endpoint for every request. Ensure that a user can only access or modify resources that they own or are explicitly authorized to access. This typically involves verifying the user's session/token against the requested resource owner's ID before returning any data. For non-owner access, proper role-based access control (RBAC) should be enforced.

findings.title: Cloudflare WAF Detected
findings.description: The website https://juice-shop.herokuapp.com is protected by Cloudflare, a widely used Content Delivery Network (CDN) and Web Application Firewall (WAF) service. Cloudflare provides protection against various web attacks, DDoS mitigation, and performance optimization. While it enhances security, it also indicates an external service managing traffic before it reaches the origin server.
findings.recommendation: Be aware that Cloudflare's WAF might block certain automated scanning tools or attack attempts. Consider using Cloudflare's own analytics and logs for insights into blocked traffic. When performing penetration testing, understand that tests will first interact with Cloudflare's security layers. Techniques to bypass Cloudflare's protection might be necessary to reach the origin server directly.

findings.title: SQL Injection Vulnerability
findings.description: A SQL Injection vulnerability was identified in a search parameter, allowing for the potential extraction of sensitive database information or modification of records. This could lead to data breaches or unauthorized access.
findings.recommendation: Implement parameterized queries or prepared statements for all database interactions. Ensure robust input validation and sanitization on all user-supplied data. Avoid concatenating user input directly into SQL queries.
findings.poc: GET /rest/products/search?q=a%27%20OR%201=1--%0A HTTP/1.1 (observed database error or altered results)

findings.title: Broken Authentication - Default/Weak Credentials
findings.description: It was possible to authenticate with default or easily guessable credentials (e.g., 'admin@juice-sh.op' / 'admin123') to gain administrative access to the application. This allows full control over the application's data and functionality.
findings.recommendation: Enforce strong password policies, implement multi-factor authentication (MFA), and ensure no default credentials are shipped with the application. Regularly audit user accounts for weak passwords.
findings.poc: POST /rest/user/login with {'email': 'admin@juice-sh.op', 'password': 'admin123'} (replace with actual default/weak credentials found)

findings.title: Cross-Site Scripting (XSS) Vulnerability
findings.description: A reflected Cross-Site Scripting (XSS) vulnerability was found in a user-controlled input field, allowing an attacker to inject malicious client-side scripts. This could lead to session hijacking, defacement, or redirection of users.
findings.recommendation: Implement proper output encoding for all user-supplied data before rendering it in HTML. Utilize a Content Security Policy (CSP) to mitigate the impact of XSS attacks. Validate and sanitize all inputs.
findings.poc: Injecting <script>alert('XSS')</script> into search fields or user profile inputs and observing execution.

findings.title: Insecure Direct Object Reference (IDOR)
findings.description: An Insecure Direct Object Reference (IDOR) vulnerability was identified, allowing an authenticated user to view or modify other users' order details by simply changing the order ID in the URL or API request without proper authorization checks.
findings.recommendation: Implement robust authorization checks at the server-side for all requests accessing resources. Use indirect references (e.g., UUIDs or GUIDs) instead of sequential IDs for sensitive objects. Ensure users can only access resources they are authorized for.
findings.poc: Logged in as User A, access /rest/order/123. Change '123' to '124' (User B's order) and observe access.

findings.title: Information Disclosure via robots.txt
findings.description: The robots.txt file discloses several directories and files (e.g., /ftp, /swagger-ui.html) that are not intended for public indexing or exposure. While not directly exploitable, this provides attackers with valuable information about the application's structure and potential attack vectors.
findings.recommendation: Review the contents of robots.txt and remove any sensitive or internal paths. Ensure that sensitive areas are protected by proper access controls and not solely reliant on obscurity.

findings.title: Subdomain Takeover
findings.description: The subdomain shop.juice-shop.herokuapp.com has a CNAME record pointing to a non-existent Heroku application ('dangling-shop-app-123.herokuapp.com'). An attacker can register this Heroku application name and claim the subdomain, allowing them to host arbitrary content, conduct phishing attacks, or exploit trust associated with the original domain.
findings.recommendation: To remediate this vulnerability, either remove the CNAME record for shop.juice-shop.herokuapp.com if it is no longer in use, or point it to an active and controlled Heroku application. Alternatively, register a Heroku application with the name 'dangling-shop-app-123' to reclaim ownership of the resource.

findings.description: The response from https://juice-shop.herokuapp.com is missing the 'Strict-Transport-Security' security header.
findings.recommendation: Add the 'Strict-Transport-Security' header to all server responses.
